# Texas AI Dispatch

Owner instruction from October 20th, 2026. config/review_limit.json imposes a hard maximum of
five paid editorial review rounds per video, including code, phone, pivot, retry and correction
attempts. Reserve the final timed phone review inside those five. No recovery allowance,
script pivot or renamed mechanism can extend the limit. After diminishing returns or the cap,
freeze the strongest credible cut and finish the existing native, audiovisual, three-scorer
and delivery path once. Do not reopen creative editing from those final checks. At that finishing boundary,
the existing bounded route can retain an original independently classified surface-finish
rejection; source, rights, minimum action, comprehension, pacing, closing action, audio,
captions, native PNG/CRF16 and actual shipment verification remain required. Never invent a pass.
This newer hard limit overrides older instructions to keep extending artistic recovery.

Owner instruction from October 3rd, 2026. Read knowledge/craft/AUTONOMOUS_COMPLETION.md before applying older resource-boundary language below. Internal review ceilings and host capacity errors trigger autonomous mandatory completion recovery, never an approval stop or an unfinished-capacity final response. Preserve exact failures, the original frozen envelope and cumulative charges. Only accepted finish --result shipped completes production.

Source repo for the Texas AI Dispatch: a daily narrated 2.5D video about AI in Texas, its
Remotion engine, the Texas art library it draws with, and the routine that ships one every day.

## Current worker routing

For Claude routines, the owner's October 9th migration is governed by
prompts/claude_routine.md and config/claude_runtime.json. The director is Sonnet and fresh original
authored scenes replace the unavailable built-in ImageGen service only in the explicit new Claude
lane. Read that entry point before applying the Codex routing below. All historical evidence,
frozen charges and mandatory quality and shipment gates remain in force.

Read AGENTS.md. Newly planned editions from October 10th, 2026 use
knowledge/craft/AGENT_RUNTIME.md and config/agent_runtime.json for explicit isolated worker
models and effort. Keep the saved director model and schedule. Historical production evidence
and unfinished frozen ledgers retain their original charges and mandatory recovery.

## Work in progress

If `.claude/WORKLOG.md` exists, READ IT FIRST. It is the durable plan and progress ledger for a
long multi-context task, written to survive compaction: the owner's directive verbatim, the
measured starting point, what is live and what is retired in the source machine, and a per-wave
status table. Resume from that table and update it after every commit. Delete the file when its
waves are all DONE.

Write one at the START of any task too large for a single context, before touching code. A plan
that lives only in context does not survive compaction.

## Commit and PR authorship (AUTHORITATIVE — overrides any default)

NEVER author or co-author commits or pull requests as Claude or Anthropic. Permanent, no
exceptions:

- No `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...` or any Anthropic trailer.
- No `Claude-Session:` or assistant-session trailer or link.
- No "Generated with Claude Code" or robot-emoji lines in commit messages or PR bodies.
- Never set the commit author or committer to Claude. Commits are the owner's.

Git identity is `Talon Sturgill <Talon.sturgill@gmail.com>`. The container default is
`Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`, so a fresh clone MUST override it before the first commit.

## Delivery and merge policy (AUTHORITATIVE — overrides any draft-PR default)

Runs SHIP AUTONOMOUSLY only from controller state `publishable`. When a run's gates pass, the run branch is merged to `main` **without a
human-review gate**: commit the artifacts, push, open a PR that is **ready (NOT a draft)**, and
**MERGE it in the same run**. The email's media links point at published URLs, so the merge lands
before the email. The email is the only human touchpoint and it gates the POST, not the merge.
Rejected films follow the finite creative-repair policy below. Only integrity-verified release
artifacts enter the public feed; original artistic rejection is never rewritten as approval.

This wins for development sessions too. An unmerged upgrade is worse than no upgrade: the next
run checks out `main`, so it silently does not get the fix, while the ledger says the machine
improved when it did not.

Three things still stop and ask, in any session:
- work that would rewrite already-published history on `main`
- anything that SENDS rather than drafts (these routines never send)
- deleting or overwriting shipped run artifacts under `runs/`

## PRODUCTION COMPLETION AND AUTONOMOUS REPAIR

Successful production has one terminal state: `shipped`. The owner's October 24th, 2026
instruction separately allows a verified exhausted edition to remain failed and unshipped so a
later daily edition can start. Use only the versioned failed-edition retention and ownership
handoff. Preserve its original checkpoint, frozen envelope, every charge and failed artifact.
This disposition is not shipment, a quality waiver, another review, or a fresh budget for the
same date. The normal five-review maximum never increases. An active publisher remains protected.

A passing exact-film panel or the independently
evidenced bounded creative route authorizes publication through `finish --result publishable`, which leaves production open in
`publishing`. Completion requires merged exact-head green CI in both repositories,
the matching Pages deployment, permanent media serving the reviewed bytes,
canonical phone playback through Computer Use, and a correctly addressed,
read-back Gmail draft carrying DRAFT and no SENT label.

A rejection before the finite creative limit remains active repair. The owner has authorized
autonomous completion; stopping for creative approval is prohibited. Preserve the
last playable native film and exact reviewer evidence, diagnose all current defects,
then open one evidence-bound repair batch. Keep usage charged. Every paid call and
render is still reserved before it starts. A batch never changes a score or original verdict.

For editions from September 29, 2026, use `config/creative_release.json` and
`knowledge/craft/BOUNDED_CREATIVE_RELEASE.md`: at most three creative repair rounds. From September 30, independently classified
technical-integrity corrections remain charged but do not count as creative rounds.
The dated minimum picture-action checks cannot be deferred; choose a credible treatment early.
Stop earlier when another full correction would consume reserved mandatory completion review
capacity. Finish the best available complete cut, obtain every required independent exact-film
review, and ship autonomously. Only explicitly assessed artistic defects can use this route.
Source truth, rights, legibility, comprehension, native picture presence, audio/caption integrity,
provider provenance and exact delivery proof remain required. Record `bounded_creative_release`
and all retained failures, even when a later panel score clears the unchanged rubric.

Run `run_controller.py begin-repair --plan out/dispatch/repair-plan.json` before
editing. The plan records root_cause, repair, mechanism_change, expected_visible_result,
failure_evidence and failure_evidence_sha256, plus changed_inputs containing path,
before_path and before_sha256. Retain the actual baseline files. Reserve the reboard,
change the named production inputs, fill their after_sha256 values, and run
`run_controller.py authorize-repair --plan out/dispatch/repair-plan.json`.
The plan's resources map requests only the calls needed for this correction.
For a direction-only correction after a failed audible take, set `repair_scope` to
`narration-performance` and request only `tts_calls` with at most two calls. Begin before
editing `vo_direction.json`; retain the failed take and baseline. Only the plan's
`after_sha256` may then change. This scope binds script, board, claims, fetched sources
and renderer, needs no reboard, and grants no visual reviews. Script or visual edits
use the standard scope. Fresh soundcheck and exact-film phone gates still apply.
The controller limits each batch, checks changed bytes, refuses repeated use of a
failed attempt, and preserves all earlier charges. Three scorers remain one atomic
panel. After two rejections of the same mechanism, change the mechanism or select
a source-backed filmable angle before another attempt.

For an independently diagnosed excerpt-context rejection, `review-context` may expand
only `cinema.hero_scene_id` and `hero_passage_end_scene_id`. Follow the exact evidence
and frozen dependency procedure in prompts/phases/repair.md. It charges one reboard,
native rendering and fresh hero review within the existing envelope, without new critics
or a creative round. It does not change the film or approve any rejected evidence.

A checkpoint is crash recovery, never completion. `package_review_run.sh` saves the
film and evidence with the controller still active. Resume that edition until it ships or the
verified exhausted-failure handoff retains it under the October 24th policy above.
The legacy needs_review outcome is refused in production. Reopen a legacy stopped
controller without resetting usage. Missing external access leaves work incomplete;
record the real evidence and next executable step without claiming delivery.

Run `python3 scripts/run_controller.py pending` at wake before creating an edition.
Host reviewer capacity is a transport failure. Follow prompts/phases/review-availability.md
to complete the same independent role through the configured provider, charging each request
within the original frozen envelope. Protect that recovery path in production-budget before
creative work. Preserve actual rejected verdicts and never replace them through this route.
Resume the returned eligible active worktree and its ledger before starting another date.
Exclude a retained failed edition only through the current verified failure catalog, never
because a filename, UI badge, elapsed day or agent-written summary says it is done.
Preserve unrelated changes in place and use an isolated clean checkout for tooling
repairs. Never delete a ledger or substitute a fresh budget.

`owner-override` and blanket preship bypass remain unavailable. Native rendering, hero review,
all three exact-byte audiovisual lenses, caption alignment, audio measurement and every
integrity/delivery check remain required. The bounded route changes only artistic release
eligibility; it never fabricates a reviewer pass or substitutes for completed shipment.

## The two laws of drawing Texas

From `TexasAIDocket/knowledge/shared/TEXAS_VERNACULAR.md`, and they govern every frame. It
lives in the sibling repo because the two products draw the same Texas, and this file used to
cite it as `knowledge/texas/VERNACULAR.md` HERE, which does not exist and never has. A scorer
went looking for the source every art decision is supposed to trace to and could not find it.

**That doc says of itself that its research pass was truncated in delivery and only its
addenda arrived**, and its own closing section lists what is still owed: the per-region light,
vegetation, buildings and vehicles. That gap is not academic. It is exactly where this show
keeps getting marked down, because a region with no drawing notes of its own inherits another
region's drawing, which is the first law broken by omission rather than by choice.

**One. A Texan forgives a stylized drawing. A Texan does not forgive being told they live
somewhere they don't.** Style is free. Place is not. The Panhandle and Houston do not share a
green. A story set in Reeves County does not get Hill Country limestone.

**Two. Build the cast demographically FIRST, before any episode needs it.** A vector library gets
built in the order it is needed, and the first character authored becomes the default reach
forever. Left alone, that default is a white man in a hat. Cowboys belong here and the base cast
opens with a rancher in a straw hat and pearl snaps. Cowboys ONLY do not. **A hat is real on a
rancher at a sale barn and a costume on a Houston software executive, and the library knows the
difference.**

Corollaries that are hard rules:

- **Facial variation lives in shape language applied evenly across all characters.** Skin tone is
  a fill value that never changes the line work. In a thick-outline idiom, feature exaggeration
  slides toward caricature without anyone intending it.
- **Six Flags Over Texas is retired as a motif.** One of the six is the Confederate flag. Use the
  Republic-era and current Lone Star only.
- **Lotería imagery and Day of the Dead iconography are appropriation, not shared culture.** Do
  not use them. Talavera tile geometry as a pattern system is fine.
- **Nothing is symmetric.** A hat crease is hand-shaped and lopsided. A mesquite is never
  balanced. A windmill fan is a full disc but the tail vane swings.
- **Maintained but worn.** A rust drip, a dent, a leaning post, a missing letter. Not new, not
  ruined.
- **The county's region is drawn behind every current film** (October 9th, 2026). From the date in
  `video-engine/src/modern/placePlates.json`, `modern/PlaceStage.tsx` draws each scene's region from
  a plate baked once per region, outdoors as the whole frame and indoors through a window. An
  episode never paints a full-frame background over it, and `scripts/place_check.py --render`
  measures that the region shows in every shot. MODERN_FILM.md has the account.

## The engine

**Remotion + React + TypeScript is the production engine.** Use SVG for exact diagrams and
editorial overlays. The owner authorized a dimensional and hybrid lane on September 23rd, 2026.
Use `config/creative_production.json` from September 29, 2026; earlier editions retain `config/cinematic_production.json`. Read `knowledge/craft/CREATIVE_DIRECTION.md`. Choose the medium from the sourced action and inspected pictures; there is no 3D opening or runtime quota under the new policy. Three.js through `@remotion/three`, when chosen, must draw original geometry, optical surfaces, physically
motivated lighting and camera moves. `lib/cinema/CinematicStage.tsx` supplies the shared studio
and `lib/cinema/motion.ts` supplies stateless motion. Read

1	When the only server at Wok and Karahi in Spring walked out, who was going to take the order?
2	The family didn't post a job ad. They put an AI host named Haniya at the front of the house.
3	A guest scans a code at the table, taps or talks to order, and pays from a phone.
4	Nothing is cooked until the order is paid for.
5	The same host answers the phone, even when the restaurant is closed.
6	The owner says the restaurant now saves or wins back $9,650 a month, and that's his own count.
7	FOX 26 reports that kitchen staff now get all of the tips.
8	Federal rules allow a tip pool with cooks when the employer takes no tip credit. No report says whether this restaurant takes one.
9	One customer said QR codes don't suit people like her mother.
10	So software now takes the order, and who gets the tip rests on the owner's word.

I can't reproduce the full regulation verbatim here. Quotes from source documents are limited to 125 characters each, so I'll summarize each subsection in my own words and quote only short key phrases. The full text is at the LII page you provided.

**29 CFR § 531.54 - Tip pooling (summary)**

- **(a) Monies counted as tips:** When employees split tips, such as waiters giving part of their tips to a busser, each person's retained share counts as their own tips under the FLSA. The same applies when an employer collects tips only for record-keeping or to redistribute them under an employee-agreed formula. The regulation also states that "Section 3(m)(2)(A) does not impose a maximum contribution percentage on mandatory tip pools."

- **(b) Prohibition against keeping tips:** The rule against employers keeping tips applies whether or not the employer takes a tip credit. Employers cannot require employees to share tips with managers, supervisors, or employers. Requiring sharing with other tip-eligible employees does not violate this rule. An employer that collects and redistributes tips does not violate the rule if it distributes them by the regular payday for the relevant workweek or pay period. If the amount can't be determined before payroll is processed, tips must be distributed as soon as practicable after that payday.

- **(c) Employers that take a tip credit:** Employers taking a tip credit may require tip pool contributions only from employees who customarily and regularly receive tips. They must notify employees of any required contribution amount and can take a tip credit only for the tips each employee actually receives. They may not keep employees' tips for other purposes, receive tips from the pool, or let managers and supervisors receive them.

- **(d) Employers that do not take a tip credit:** Employers paying the full minimum wage without a tip credit may require pooling that includes employees who don't customarily receive tips, such as dishwashers and cooks. Employers still cannot receive tips from the pool or let supervisors and managers share in it.

**Citation:** 85 FR 86789, Dec. 30, 2020, as amended at 86 FR 52986, Sept. 24, 2021.

For the exact wording of any subsection, see the LII page at the source URL. For questions about how these rules apply to a specific situation, consult a qualified employment or legal professional.

**Owners and managers keeping tips (Paragraph 5):**
- "Section 203(m)(2)(B) of the FLSA makes it clear that owners and managers cannot keep employee tips, under any circumstances." (124 characters)

The full sentence exceeds 125 characters, so I've split it into two quotes:
- "inclusion of cooks, dishwashers, and similar employees in a tip pool" (68 characters)
- "if the employer pays tipped employees at least the full minimum wage" (69 characters)

3	 Spring restaurant using AI to simplify ordering 
4	 AI is transforming the dining experience at Wok & Karahi, a family-run Asian restaurant in Spring! FOX 26 reporter Olivia Dance visited the restaurant to get a first-hand look at the change that took place in just 24 hours after a server walked out.
5	 The Brief
6	 After its sole server walked out, Wok & Karahi, a family-run Asian restaurant in Spring, replaced front-of-house staff with an AI platform named Haniya. 
7	 100% of customer tips now go directly to the chef and kitchen staff, while ordering is handled via phone, QR codes, and pre-payment. 
8	 The restaurant reports saving thousands per month now. 
9	 SPRING, Texas - Two months ago, the sole server at Wok & Karahi, a family-run Chinese, Indian, and Pakistani restaurant, walked off the job. Rather than shutting down or rushing to post job listings, owner Abbas Zoeb —a former Google software engineer— decided to replace the position with an AI software named Haniya.
10	 "It started out of desperation," said Zoeb. "We could not keep begging one person to show up. Now nobody has to, and our guests and our team are better off for it."
11	 Restaurant's new AI platform
12	 Implementing AI:
13	 Within 24 hours, a virtual host, QR codes and a new pre-pay ordering system took over operations. The digital server speaks seven languages and answers the phone even when the restaurant is closed.
14	 As many independent dining spots across the country struggle with staffing shortages, Wok & Karahi offers a glimpse at the future of fast-casual dining. 
15	 By the numbers:
16	 Today, Zoeb claims the restaurant is saving or winning back $9,650 a month. With about $3,500 of those savings coming from the server salary. 
17	 He says the remaining $6,150 comes from operational efficiencies and reclaimed revenue. 
18	 Kitchen staff and the chef now get 100-percent of customer tips.
19	 The cost to run the AI software is about $300 a month or roughly $10 a day.
20	 Will this work for other businesses?
21	 Casual vs. fine dining limits:
22	 While the setup has stabilized operations at Wok & Karahi, experts note that automation isn’t a one-size-fits-all solution for the hospitality industry. 
23	 Professor Dietrich von Biedenfeld, Supply Chain Manager at the University of Houston Downtown, says: "This seems like a very effective tool for a fast-food restaurant or a quick lunch spot, but for fine dining, the AI is only as good as the prompts."
24	 For casual concepts facing severe labor pressures, Wok & Karahi demonstrates how software can safeguard small business margins. However, the broader question remains whether diners will embrace AI efficiency over human hospitality—or if full automation will remain strictly suited for high-volume, quick-service environments.
25	 The Source: We spoke with Wok & Karahi owner Abbas Zoeb about the new AI software and Professor Dietrich von Biedenfeld.

240	 No Servers, No Host, and No Phone Calls: AI Takes Over at a Halal Restaurant in Houston, Texas
241	 L-R, A table of Wok & Karahi dishes, Chinese and Pakistani side by side. And Haniya, the restaurant's AI host, who answers the phone and serves guests at the table. 
242	 By Muslim Mirror 
243	 October 19, 2026 
244	 SPRING, Texas – Two months ago the only server at Wok & Karahi, a family-run zabihah halal restaurant north of Houston, walked out. The family did not post a job ad. Within 24 hours every table had a QR code, an AI host named Haniya was answering the phone, and every order was being paid for before it reached the kitchen.
245	 Haniya, the restaurant’s AI server, greets a returning guest by name on the table menu. 
246	 Nobody has been hired into that job since 
247	 “It started out of desperation,” said Abbas Zoeb, who runs the restaurant with his family. “We could not keep begging one person to show up. Now nobody has to, and our guests and our team are better off for it.”
248	 America’s biggest chains are racing to do the same thing. Yum Brands says voice AI now takes orders at more than 890 Taco Bell drive-thrus. McDonald’s has said it will bring AI to all 43,000 of its restaurants. The National Restaurant Association’s 2026 industry report found that 80 percent of US restaurants were short at least one position last year. Those chains have engineering teams and large budgets. Wok & Karahi, which serves Hakka-style Chinese food alongside Indian and Pakistani dishes, has one family.
249	 A server you can talk to 
250	 A guest sits down and scans the code on the table. Haniya greets them and asks which language they want: English, Spanish, Urdu, Hindi, Gujarati, Punjabi or Arabic.
251	 Haniya, the restaurant’s AI server, greets a returning guest by name on the table menu. 
252	 When a regular opens the menu, she greets them by name: “Welcome back. What can I get you?”
253	 From there the guest can tap through the menu, or talk to her the way they would talk to a waiter. Say “chicken chow mein” and the dish opens on screen, chicken is selected, and she says “Adding chicken chow mein” as the price updates. Ask what goes well with the karahi and she suggests a pairing, based on what other guests actually order together. She asks only the questions the kitchen needs answered, one at a time, and tells the guest what she added. A note like “no onions” or “nut allergy” prints on the kitchen ticket word for word, because the guest entered it. For guests who find apps hard, older guests especially, there is nothing to learn: hold the button and say what you want.
254	 Haniya also remembers people. The same host answers the phone, the website and the table, and she knows each guest’s past orders, favourites and rewards across all of them. A regular is treated like a regular. A few hours after a direct order, the guest gets a thank-you text asking how it went. Pickup guests get a text the moment their food is ready.
255	 Guests pay from their own phone with Apple Pay or Google Pay. There is no waiting for the check, and no dine-and-dash, because nothing is cooked until it is paid for.
256	 The work nobody sees 
257	 What the guest sees is the small part. Behind it, the restaurant runs on software the family built with AI tools.
258	 The phone answers 24 hours a day, including when the restaurant is closed. Late-night catering callers used to find nobody there and take their order elsewhere. Now Haniya takes the request, answers the question or books the order for the next day. She offers an add-on on every call, and about four in ten callers say yes. The AI phone line costs about $5 a day to run.
259	 Orders from seven places – the counter, the phone, the tables, the website, DoorDash, Uber Eats and Grubhub – land on one screen in the back. Every advertising dollar is traced to the order it brought in. The owner gets a text on every table order and an alert if a ticket fails to print. Every call is recorded and reviewed, and each week the spots where guests got stuck are fixed.
260	 The money 
261	 By the family’s own count, the system is worth about $9,650 a month. That includes the server’s $3,500 monthly salary, about $2,000 for each day they used to close when nobody could cover a shift, family members no longer pulled in to work the floor, catering that no longer goes to competitors, and fewer wrong orders.
262	 The tips changed too. The cooks who make the food now share in them.
263	 The question everyone asks 
264	 Does it take jobs? At Wok & Karahi, the job that went away was the one the family could not keep filled. The people who stayed are calmer during the rush, because one person is no longer answering the phone, taking orders, running payments and greeting the door at the same time.
265	 Zoeb now builds the same kind of system for other independent restaurants through his company, AZ Restaurant Partners ( azrestaurantpartners.com ).
266	 Wok & Karahi is at 3422 FM 2920 Rd, Unit 120, Spring, Texas 77388. wokandkarahitexas.com

28	 HARRIS COUNTY, Texas – What if the next time you went out to eat, there was no one to take your order — and your tip went straight to the people cooking your food?
29	 That’s exactly what’s happening at Wok and Karahi, a restaurant in Spring that turned to artificial intelligence after struggling to stay open.
30	 The restaurant is changing how it serves customers, and Head Chef Edwin Hernandez says the atmosphere has shifted because of it.
31	 “It’s humble, you know, to wake up every morning and thinking I’m coming to work to a place where our customers not only happy. Us as well,” Hernandez said.
32	 How it works
33	 Instead of waiting for a server, customers are guided to a tablet-based ordering system.
34	 “They don’t have to come and wait for the server,” Hernandez said.
35	 Owner Abbas Manakibwala developed the software himself. It goes by the name Haniya.
36	 Free parking at Houston’s Galleria garages will end. Here’s how much shoppers will pay 
37	 “We point them to this tablet,” Manakibwala said. “She can better serve you more custom way. So here, if you’re dining in, you just select how many people, and it tells you which table to go.”
38	 The AI goes beyond just taking orders. It can also predict when the restaurant will be busy and help streamline operational costs.
39	 Not everyone is convinced
40	 For some first-time customers, the switch to QR code menus has come with a learning curve.
41	 “I would really like give it another shot. But it’s just the QR code thing, I think it’s not very convenient for every kind of people like my mom, she’s not like a QR code person,” said customer Amna Shaikh.
42	 Voters near Moody Park worried about police presence. We asked METRO about it. 
43	 Despite the hesitation, Hernandez says the benefits in the kitchen are hard to ignore.
44	 “It saves us time and the dish is more, it’s fresh,” he said.
45	 For the owners, the move is also expected to pay off financially. They project the AI system will save them more than $115,000.

10	 § 531.54 Tip pooling.
11	 (a) Monies counted as tips. Where employees practice tip splitting, as where waiters give a portion of their tips to the busser, both the amounts retained by the waiters and those given the bussers are considered tips of the individuals who retain them, in applying the provisions of sections 3(m)(2)(A) and 3(t). Similarly, where an accounting is made to an employer for his or her information only or in furtherance of a pooling arrangement whereby the employer redistributes the tips to the employees upon some basis to which they have mutually agreed among themselves, the amounts received and retained by each individual as his or her own are counted as his or her tips for purposes of the Act. Section 3(m)(2)(A) does not impose a maximum contribution percentage on mandatory tip pools.
12	 (b) Prohibition against keeping tips —(1) Meaning of “keep.” Section 3(m)(2)(B)'s prohibition against keeping tips applies regardless of whether an employer takes a tip credit. Section 3(m)(2)(B) expressly prohibits employers from requiring employees to share tips with managers or supervisors, as defined in § 531.52(b)(2) , or employers, as defined in 29 U.S.C. 203(d) . An employer does not violate section 3(m)(2)(B)'s prohibition against keeping tips if it requires employees to share tips with other employees who are eligible to receive tips.
13	 (2) Full and prompt distribution of tips. An employer that facilitates tip pooling by collecting and redistributing employees' tips does not violate section 3(m)(2)(B)'s prohibition against keeping tips if it fully distributes any tips the employer collects no later than the regular payday for the workweek in which the tips were collected, or when the pay period covers more than a single workweek, the regular payday for the period in which the workweek ends. To the extent that it is not possible for an employer to ascertain the amount of tips that have been received or how tips should be distributed prior to processing payroll, tips must be distributed to employees as soon as practicable after the regular payday.
14	 (c) Employers that take a section 3(m)(2)(A) tip credit. When an employer takes a tip credit pursuant to section 3(m)(2)(A):
15	 (1) The employer may require an employee for whom the employer takes a tip credit to contribute tips to a tip pool only if it is limited to employees who customarily and regularly receive tips; and
16	 (2) The employer must notify its employees of any required tip pool contribution amount, may only take a tip credit for the amount of tips each employee ultimately receives, and may not retain any of the employees' tips for any other purpose.
17	 (3) An employer may not receive tips from such a tip pool and may not allow managers and supervisors to receive tips from the tip pool.
18	 (d) Employers that do not take a section 3(m)(2)(A) tip credit. An employer that pays its tipped employees the full minimum wage and does not take a tip credit may impose a tip pooling arrangement that includes dishwashers, cooks, or other employees in the establishment who are not employed in an occupation in which employees customarily and regularly receive tips. An employer may not receive tips from such a tip pool and may not allow supervisors and managers to receive tips from the tip pool.
19	 [ 85 FR 86789 , Dec. 30, 2020, as amended at 86 FR 52986 , Sept. 24, 2021]

9	 Tip-Pooling / Tip-Sharing
10	 The U.S. Department of Labor's position is that tip-pooling / tip-sharing arrangements are permissible as long as the employees sharing in the tips have somehow participated in serving the customers who left the tips. Courts cases regarding tip-sharing arrangements focus on whether the employee interacted with the customer, assisted in providing the customer with a pleasurable dining experience, and/or provided "direct table service" before or during the meal, while the customer was seated. It is a good practice to put the tip-sharing policy in writing and have everyone acknowledge it.
11	 DOL regulation 29 C.F.R. § 531.54 sets out the requirements for a valid tip-pooling arrangement, including a prohibition against sharing of tips with managers, supervisors, or owners, distribution of tips no later than the regular payday for the workweek in question, limitation of the tip pool to "employees who customarily and regularly receive tips", notice to employees of the tip pool contribution amount, limitation of the tip credit to the amounts actually received from the pool by employees, and inclusion of cooks, dishwashers, and similar employees in a tip pool if the employer pays tipped employees at least the full minimum wage. These requirements are in addition to the other requirements outlined in 29 C.F.R. § 531.59(b) for taking the tip credit for tipped employees.
12	 DOL Field Operations Handbook § 30d04: Tip pooling.
13	 The requirement that an employee must retain all tips does not preclude tip-splitting or pooling arrangements among employees who customarily and regularly receive tips. The following occupations have been recognized as falling within the eligible category:
14	 waiters
15	 bellhops
16	 counter personnel who serve customers
17	 busboys/girls (server helpers)
18	 service bartenders
19	It is not required that all employees who share in tips must themselves receive tips from customers. The amounts retained by the employees who actually receive the tips, and those given to other pool participants are considered the tips of the individuals who retain them, in applying the provisions of sections [203(m)] and [203(t)].
20	 A valid tip-pooling arrangement cannot require employees who actually receive tips to contribute a greater percentage of their tips than is customary and reasonable. For enforcement purposes, Wage and Hour will not question contributions to a pool where the net amount of tips contribute (after return of any tips from the pool) does not exceed 15 percent of the employee's tips. However, only those tips that are in excess of tips used for tip credit (e.g., where the maximum tip credit is taken, those in excess of 40 percent of the minimum wage) may be taken for a pool. If such requirements are met, it is not necessary that the pooling be voluntarily consented to by the employees involved (notwithstanding Reg. 531.54).
21	 Tipped employees may not be required to share their tips with employees who have not customarily and regularly participated in tip pooling arrangements. The following employee occupations would therefore not be eligible to participate:
22	 janitors
23	 dishwashers
24	 chefs or cooks
25	 laundry room attendants
26	However, it does not appear that Congress ... intended to prevent tipped employees from deciding, free from any coercion whatever ..., what to do with their tips, including sharing them with whichever co-workers they please. Tips given to such co-workers as are listed in this subsection may not, however, be used as a tip credit.
27	 ... In the case of host/hostesses, head waiters, or seater/greeters and other employees not referred to above, facts should be developed showing the practices regarding their sharing of tips in the locality and type of establishment involved.
28	 Two DOL opinion letters address this issue:
29	 Customer-greeting chefs are tipped employees: https://www.dol.gov/sites/dolgov/files/WHD/legacy/files/2008_12_19_18_FLSA.pdf 
30	 Barbacks are tipped employees: https://www.dol.gov/sites/dolgov/files/WHD/legacy/files/2009_01_15_12_FLSA.pdf 
31	 Section 203(m)(2)(B) of the FLSA makes it clear that owners and managers cannot keep employee tips, under any circumstances. That would include tips left by customers in tip jars, which the DOL and the courts would consider employee tips under the rationale that customers who leave tips in tip jars do so with the belief that the tips will end up in the hands of the staff who served them, not the owner or manager of the restaurant. The only time that an owner or manager would be permitted to keep a tip would be if the evidence showed that a customer meant the tip for the personal benefit of the owner or manager.
32	 Service charges or gratuities charged by an employer are not tips - see 29 C.F.R. § 531.55 - "A compulsory charge for service, such as 15 percent of the amount of the bill, imposed on a customer by an employer's establishment, is not a tip and, even if distributed by the employer to its employees, cannot be counted as a tip received in applying the provisions of sections 3(m)(2)(A) and 3(t) ." However, the same regulation points out that if distributed to employees, gratuities count toward any non-tipped wages that are due.
33	 Chau v. Starbucks , 94 Cal.Rptr.3d 593 3 (Cal. Ct. App., 4th Dist., July 2, 2009) - Section 351 (the California tipped employee statute) does not contain any language prohibiting an employer from equitably dividing tips placed in a collective box among the employees who provided the service.
34	 Budrow v. Dave & Busters of Calif., Inc. , 90 Cal.Rptr.3d 239 (Cal. Ct. App., 2nd Dist., Mar. 2, 2009) - Bartenders who poured or mixed drinks that were brought to restaurant patrons at their tables could participate in tip pools established pursuant to statute making gratuities property of employees to whom they were paid, even if bartenders did not personally bring drinks to tables.
35	 Hosts are tipped employees: Kilgore v. Outback Steakhouse of Florida, Inc., a/k/a FMI Restaurants, Inc. , 160 F.3d 294 (6th Cir. 1998): "an employer must inform its employees of its intent to take a tip credit toward the employer's minimum wage obligation." Hosts at Outback are "engaged in an occupation in which [they] customarily and regularly receive . . . tips because they sufficiently interact with customers in an industry (restaurant) where undesignated tips are common." "... one court has held that a tip pool that benefits a maitre d' is permissible under the FLSA. In Dole v. Continental Cuisine, Inc. , 751 F. Supp. 799 (E.D. Ark. 1990), the district court upheld a mandatory tip pool where servers tipped out solely to a maitre d' who 'receives no tips directly from customers' and whose responsibilities included setting up the dining room, greeting and seating customers, serving the first drink to customers, and assisting servers in serving customers as needed."
36	 Etheridge v. Reins International , 91 Cal.Rptr.3d 816: The court explained that "[t]ip pools exist to minimize friction between employees and to enable the employer to manage the potential confusion about gratuities in a way that is fair to the employees."
37	 In the Ninth Circuit, the tip pooling rules apply only when a tipped employee is paid a cash wage of less than the federal minimum wage. "The FLSA does not restrict tip pooling when no tip credit is taken." ( See Cumbie v. Woody Woo, Inc ., 596 F.3d 577, 582 (9th Cir. 2010).) The 4th Circuit recently agreed with the 9th Circuit on that issue ( Trejo v. Ryman Hospitality Properties, Inc. , No. 14-cv-1485, 2015 WL 4548259 (4th Cir. July 29, 2015)).
38	 For tipped employees, it would not be legal to make deductions from tips toward a "breakage" fund. See the following two cases:
39	 Chisolm v. Gravitas Restaurant Ltd. , 2008 WL 838760 (S.D. Tex. 2008) and
40	 Bursell v. Tommy's Seafood Steakhouse , 2006 WL 3227334 (S.D. Tex. 2006).
41	 Under the OBBBA ( H.R. 1 , enacted in 2025), qualified tips (which would include an employee's share of a tip pool) and FLSA-required overtime pay are partially exempt from federal income tax (but not from other state and federal payroll taxes). Useful guidance regarding the extent to which such payments may be excluded from an employee's gross income is on the IRS website at https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/one-big-beautiful-bill-provisions (click on "No tax on tips (Section 70201)" and "No tax on overtime (Section 70202)").
42	 For information on the tip credit and overtime pay for tipped employees, click here .
43	 Go to the Employer Commissioner's Page 
44	 Go to the TWC Home Page

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Refuse a validator report that belongs to another Dispatch.
3	
4	The September 9 package once copied a still-valid September 8 report into the new run. Every
5	film gate passed because the validator file existed, but its date and findings described a
6	different story. This check binds the report to the board date and to the current claims before
7	delivery can copy it into ``runs/``.
8	"""
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	import argparse
12	from datetime import date as calendar_date
13	import json
14	import sys
15	import tempfile
16	from pathlib import Path
17	
18	# Earlier runs used different validator-report shapes. This contract starts with the run whose
19	# cross-day copy exposed the gap; history before it remains immutable rather than being rewritten
20	# to satisfy a gate that did not exist when those packages shipped.
21	CONTRACT_DATE = "2026-09-09"
22	
23	
24	def load(path: Path) -> dict:
25	    try:
26	        value = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
27	    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
28	        raise ValueError(f"{path} is not readable JSON: {exc}") from exc
29	    if not isinstance(value, dict):
30	        raise ValueError(f"{path} must contain one JSON object")
31	    return value
32	
33	
34	def check(validation_path: Path, claims_path: Path, board_path: Path | None = None,
35	          *, edition_date: str | None = None) -> list[str]:
36	    problems: list[str] = []
37	    try:
38	        validation = load(validation_path)
39	        claims = load(claims_path)
40	        if (board_path is None) == (edition_date is None):
41	            raise ValueError("supply one storyboard or an explicit early-phase edition date")
42	        if edition_date is not None:
43	            if calendar_date.fromisoformat(edition_date).isoformat() != edition_date:
44	                raise ValueError("early-phase edition date must be YYYY-MM-DD")
45	            board = {"date": edition_date}
46	        else:
47	            board = load(board_path)
48	    except ValueError as exc:
49	        return [str(exc)]
50	
51	    board_date = str(board.get("date") or "")
52	    report_date = str(validation.get("date") or "")
53	    if not board_date:
54	        problems.append("the storyboard has no date, so the validation can't be bound to a run")
55	    elif report_date != board_date:
56	        binding_label = "edition" if edition_date is not None else "storyboard"
57	        problems.append(
58	            f"validation date {report_date!r} does not match {binding_label} date {board_date!r}. "
59	            "This report belongs to a different Dispatch."
60	        )
61	
62	    current_verified = {
63	        str(claim.get("id"))
64	        for claim in claims.get("claims", [])
65	        if isinstance(claim, dict) and claim.get("verdict") == "VERIFIED" and claim.get("id")
66	    }
67	    reported = validation.get("verified_claim_ids")
68	    if not isinstance(reported, list) or not all(isinstance(item, str) for item in reported):
69	        problems.append("validation verified_claim_ids must be a list of claim ids")
70	    else:
71	        report_ids = set(reported)
72	        missing = sorted(current_verified - report_ids)
73	        unknown = sorted(report_ids - current_verified)
74	        if missing:
75	            problems.append("validation omits current verified claim ids: " + ", ".join(missing))
76	        if unknown:
77	            problems.append("validation names ids that are not current verified claims: " +
78	                            ", ".join(unknown))
79	
80	    if validation.get("result") not in {"PASS", "PASS_WITH_DROPS"}:
81	        problems.append("validation result must be PASS or PASS_WITH_DROPS before delivery")
82	    if not validation.get("source"):
83	        problems.append("validation names no source")
84	    # A complete independent PASS may have nothing to reject or correct. Requiring
85	    # invented findings contradicts the research handoff and alters the review.
86	    # Empty findings are valid only when every supplied claim is independently
87	    # verified; drops and incomplete claim sets retain the findings requirement.
88	    claim_rows = claims.get("claims")
89	    complete_pass = (
90	        validation.get("result") == "PASS"
91	        and isinstance(claim_rows, list) and bool(claim_rows)
92	        and all(isinstance(row, dict) and row.get("id")
93	                and row.get("verdict") == "VERIFIED" for row in claim_rows)
94	    )
95	    for field in ("rejected", "required_edits_applied"):
96	        value = validation.get(field)
97	        if not isinstance(value, list) or (not value and not complete_pass) or not all(
98	                isinstance(item, str) and item.strip() for item in value):
99	            problems.append(f"validation {field} must be a list of findings; only a complete "
100	                            "PASS over independently verified claims may use an empty list")
101	    state_path = validation_path.parent / 'run_state.json'
102	    if state_path.is_file():
103	        from validation_completion import source_validation_problems
104	        problems += source_validation_problems(load(state_path), validation_path.parent)
105	    return problems
106	
107	
108	def self_test() -> int:
109	    failures = 0
110	
111	    def ok(label: str, condition: bool, extra: str = "") -> None:
112	        nonlocal failures
113	        print(f"  {'ok  ' if condition else 'FAIL'}  {label}"
114	              f"{'' if condition else '  ' + extra}")
115	        if not condition:
116	            failures += 1
117	
118	    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
119	        root = Path(td)
120	        board = root / "storyboard.json"
121	        claims = root / "claims.json"
122	        validation = root / "validation.json"
123	        board.write_text(json.dumps({"date": "2026-09-09"}), encoding="utf-8")
124	        claims.write_text(json.dumps({"claims": [
125	            {"id": "c1", "verdict": "VERIFIED"},
126	            {"id": "c2", "verdict": "REJECTED"},
127	        ]}), encoding="utf-8")
128	        good = {
129	            "date": "2026-09-09",
130	            "source": "validator",
131	            "result": "PASS_WITH_DROPS",
132	            "verified_claim_ids": ["c1"],
133	            "rejected": ["an unsupported conclusion"],
134	            "required_edits_applied": ["the conclusion was removed"],
135	        }
136	        validation.write_text(json.dumps(good), encoding="utf-8")
137	        ok("a report bound to the current date and claims passes",
138	           not check(validation, claims, board))
139	        ok("the same complete report can be checked before a board exists",
140	           not check(validation, claims, edition_date="2026-09-09"))
141	        ok("early validation refuses a report from another edition",
142	           bool(check(validation, claims, edition_date="2026-09-10")))
143	        ok("early validation refuses an invalid or ambiguous date",
144	           bool(check(validation, claims, edition_date="20260909")) and
145	           bool(check(validation, claims, board, edition_date="2026-09-09")))
146	
147	        validation.write_text(json.dumps({**good, "date": "2026-09-08"}), encoding="utf-8")
148	        problems = check(validation, claims, board)
149	        ok("a prior day's report is refused", any("different Dispatch" in p for p in problems),
150	           str(problems))
151	
152	        validation.write_text(json.dumps({**good, "verified_claim_ids": ["c9"]}),
153	                              encoding="utf-8")
154	        problems = check(validation, claims, board)
155	        ok("unknown and missing claim ids are both refused",
156	           any("omits" in p for p in problems) and any("not current" in p for p in problems),
157	           str(problems))
158	        ok("early validation still refuses unknown and missing claim ids",
159	           bool(check(validation, claims, edition_date="2026-09-09")))
160	
161	        validation.write_text(json.dumps({**good, "result": "FAIL"}), encoding="utf-8")
162	        ok("a failed validation can't enter delivery", bool(check(validation, claims, board)))
163	        ok("a failed validation can't enter picture production",
164	           bool(check(validation, claims, edition_date="2026-09-09")))
165	
166	        complete_claims = {"claims": [
167	            {"id": "c1", "verdict": "VERIFIED"},
168	            {"id": "c2", "verdict": "VERIFIED"},
169	        ]}
170	        complete = {**good, "result": "PASS", "verified_claim_ids": ["c1", "c2"],
171	                    "rejected": [], "required_edits_applied": []}
172	        claims.write_text(json.dumps(complete_claims), encoding="utf-8")
173	        validation.write_text(json.dumps(complete), encoding="utf-8")
174	        ok("a complete independent PASS needs no invented rejection or edit",
175	           not check(validation, claims, board)
176	           and not check(validation, claims, edition_date="2026-09-09"))
177	        validation.write_text(json.dumps({**complete, "required_edits_applied":
178	                                         ["the spoken qualifier was corrected"]}), encoding="utf-8")
179	        ok("a complete PASS can retain real edits and an empty rejected list",
180	           not check(validation, claims, board))
181	
182	        for field in ("rejected", "required_edits_applied"):
183	            for value in (None, "none", [""], ["   "], [1]):
184	                validation.write_text(json.dumps({**complete, field: value}), encoding="utf-8")
185	                ok(f"complete PASS refuses malformed {field} {value!r}",
186	                   bool(check(validation, claims, board)))
187	            missing_field = {k: v for k, v in complete.items() if k != field}
188	            validation.write_text(json.dumps(missing_field), encoding="utf-8")
189	            ok(f"complete PASS still requires {field}", bool(check(validation, claims, board)))
190	
191	        for change in ({"verified_claim_ids": ["c1"]}, {"verified_claim_ids": ["c1", "c9"]},
192	                       {"date": "2026-09-08"}, {"result": "FAIL"},
193	                       {"result": "PASS_WITH_DROPS"}, {"source": ""}):
194	            validation.write_text(json.dumps({**complete, **change}), encoding="utf-8")
195	            ok(f"empty findings do not bypass {change!r}", bool(check(validation, claims, board)))
196	
197	        validation.write_text(json.dumps(complete), encoding="utf-8")
198	        for rows in ([], [{"id": "c1", "verdict": "VERIFIED"},
199	                         {"id": "c2", "verdict": "REJECTED"}],
200	                     [{"id": "c1", "verdict": "VERIFIED"},
201	                      {"id": "c2", "verdict": "PARTIAL"}],
202	                     [{"verdict": "VERIFIED"}], [None]):
203	            claims.write_text(json.dumps({"claims": rows}), encoding="utf-8")
204	            ok("empty findings refuse an empty, incomplete or unverified claim set",
205	               bool(check(validation, claims, board)))
206	        for rows in ([], [{"id": "c1", "verdict": "VERIFIED"},
207	                         {"id": "c2", "verdict": "REJECTED"}]):
208	            claims.write_text(json.dumps({"claims": rows}), encoding="utf-8")
209	            reported_ids = [row["id"] for row in rows if row["verdict"] == "VERIFIED"]
210	            validation.write_text(json.dumps({**complete, "verified_claim_ids": reported_ids}),
211	                                  encoding="utf-8")
212	            ok("matching ids cannot hide an empty or partly rejected claim set",
213	               bool(check(validation, claims, board)))
214	
215	    print(f"validation_check: {failures} failure(s)")
216	    return 1 if failures else 0
217	
218	
219	def main() -> int:
220	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
221	    parser.add_argument("--validation", default="out/dispatch/validation.json")
222	    parser.add_argument("--claims", default="out/dispatch/claims.json")
223	    binding = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
224	    binding.add_argument("--board", default="out/dispatch/storyboard.json")
225	    binding.add_argument("--date", help="check the source handoff before storyboarding; delivery still uses --board")
226	    parser.add_argument("--all", action="store_true",
227	                        help="check every shipped run that carries a validator report")
228	    parser.add_argument("--self-test", action="store_true")
229	    args = parser.parse_args()
230	    if args.all and args.date:
231	        parser.error("--all cannot use an early-phase --date")
232	    if args.self_test:
233	        return self_test()
234	    if args.all:
235	        problems: list[str] = []
236	        checked = 0
237	        for validation in sorted((Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "runs").glob(
238	                "????-??-??/validation.json")):
239	            if validation.parent.name < CONTRACT_DATE:
240	                continue
241	            checked += 1
242	            run = validation.parent
243	            for problem in check(validation, run / "claims.json", run / "storyboard.json"):
244	                problems.append(f"{run.name}: {problem}")
245	        if checked == 0:
246	            problems.append("no shipped validation report was found, so --all checked nothing")
247	    else:
248	        checked = 1
249	        problems = check(Path(args.validation), Path(args.claims),
250	                         None if args.date else Path(args.board), edition_date=args.date)
251	    if problems:
252	        print("validation_check: FAIL")
253	        for problem in problems:
254	            print(f"  - {problem}")
255	        return 1
256	    binding_name = "edition date" if args.date else "board"
257	    print(f"validation_check: OK — {checked} validator report(s) match their {binding_name} and claims")
258	    return 0
259	
260	
261	if __name__ == "__main__":
262	    sys.exit(main())
263

1	# Research and select
2	
3	For new Claude editions from October 16th, after controller initialization and before reserving
4	any researcher, run `python scripts/provider_availability.py --state out/dispatch/run_state.json`.
5	It precharges one tiny unscored generation request, protects the complete remaining route and
6	retains its real response. A model-list GET or credential presence cannot replace this check.
7	Current Claude source packets and plans require the successful receipt. On an actual service
8	refusal retain its charge and evidence before any research, validation or art work. HTTP 402
9	requires external credit restoration; never purchase credits or blindly repeat the failed probe.
10	Historical and already active earlier editions keep their original ledgers and evidence.
11	
12	For the Claude host, use the following input-packet/plan commands in place of the Codex
13	agent_runtime.py commands in this phase. Execute the returned agent_args with the named
14	versioned leaf only after reserving the same controller resource. Change the role and actual
15	input paths for the validator handoff; keep its independent full-source re-fetch.
16	
17	```sh
18	python scripts/claude_runtime.py input-packet --role researcher --date <date> --input <actual-docket-ledger> --input knowledge/texas/APPLICATIONS.md --out out/dispatch/researcher-packet.json
19	python scripts/claude_runtime.py plan --role researcher --packet out/dispatch/researcher-packet.json --task-name researcher --subject "<actual concrete candidate object>" --scope "Research one current source-backed Texas action and its consequence and limit" --out out/dispatch/researcher-assignment.json
20	```
21	
22	From newly planned October 20th Claude editions, the researcher plan requires the actual
23	candidate object through `--subject`. The planner screens it against the recent published
24	narrations and a separate metadata anchor before a researcher reservation. It retains a
25	hash-bound subject-screen report beside the packet, including a refusal. The validator plan
26	repeats this free check on the bound selection's actual movement.object before its reservation.
27	Renamed entity labels cannot hide the same physical subject. A literal phrase alone or shared
28	channel terminology does not reject a fresh story. The existing entity gate and independent
29	full-source validation remain required. On a repeat retain the refusal and choose a fresh
30	candidate autonomously, before buying a worker. Missing archive evidence requires restoring
31	the committed file, never skipping the check. Historical ledgers and active October 19 work
32	retain their original policy and charges. Never stop a paid worker to tidy an avoidable choice;
33	screen the next subject before starting it.
34	
35	Read knowledge/texas/APPLICATIONS.md, the researcher brief and config/production_actions.json.
36	Start with current Docket movements, then fetch primary evidence for the application and its
37	human consequence. Read full pages before citing them. A headline or search snippet is a lead.
38	
39	For newly planned editions from October 3rd, read the visual-storytelling selector and
40	knowledge/craft/visual-storytelling/viewer-plan.md. Screen the reporting angle through the actual picture access before choosing
41	the story. A candidate earns its place through a recognizable task, transformation or changed
42	choice. Ask the existing researchers for the strongest useful image, the missing picture and
43	the strongest source limitation in their existing filmability rationale. Keep the same bounded
44	research pass and compact role assignments; no additional outlet-study pass is required daily.
45	
46	For newly planned editions under agent_runtime.json, prefer one promising beat. Retain the
47	actual researcher response as out/dispatch/research.json. Before reserving, prepare its source
48	packet with the actual Docket ledger path and the current applications reference:
49	
50	```sh
51	python scripts/agent_runtime.py --input-packet --role researcher --edition <date> --input <actual-docket-ledger> --input knowledge/texas/APPLICATIONS.md --out out/dispatch/researcher-packet.json
52	python scripts/agent_runtime.py --plan --role researcher --packet out/dispatch/researcher-packet.json --task-name researcher --scope "Research one current source-backed Texas application and its filmable action, consequence and limit" --out out/dispatch/researcher-assignment.json
53	```
54	
55	Execute the returned spawn_args only after the existing reservation. Expand research only
56	when source or filmability screening requires another angle; never spawn the maximum by habit.
57	
58	```sh
59	python scripts/dedupe.py list --days 30
60	python scripts/run_controller.py consume --resource research_agents --note "<distinct beat>"
61	```
62	
63	Spawn the accepted `researcher` agents in one bounded parallel batch, after reserving each.
64	Use as many independent angles as the decision needs, up to the configured normal target.
65	The target is not a minimum. Workers do not recursively delegate. Reuse valid current research.
66	
67	Choose one dated Texas action: who did what, where, when, what changed, what happens next,
68	and who can still act. Prefer work in the oilfield, farm/ranch/water, transport, medicine,
69	public research, emergencies or manufacturing. Build-out and policy are individual beats,
70	not substitutes for the application layer. Search beyond the first candidate when its pictures
71	cannot explain its action. Respect the dedupe window and beat caps.

74	actual scope. Researcher filmability.action_support records a demonstrated action_id or an
75	inspected source asset, its factual source, scope_fit and rights evidence. Apply the dated medium policy in CREATIVE_DIRECTION.md; from September 29 the opening
76	may use the strongest authenticated medium. Record selected.visual_stakes and its fetched source URLs. Unsupported synthetic human performance is a reason to select a filmable sourced angle now. If the starter catalog and inspected footage do not supply the central action, use the bounded source-backed proposal in DAILY_PRODUCTION.md. Record the actual source, module, disclosure and visible consequence before candidate admission; a concept alone is not approval.
77	
78	Write out/dispatch/story_selection.json using schema dispatch_story_selection/1 and edition_date.

80	event_type/date, why_today, consequence, application_change, counter_image, earned_take,

717	```sh
718	python scripts/claude_runtime.py phone-packet --packet out/dispatch/critic-packet.json --state out/dispatch/run_state.json --sequence-a out/dispatch/openings/motion-a/index.json --sequence-b out/dispatch/openings/motion-b/index.json --out out/dispatch/phone-critic-packet.json
719	```
720	
721	Plan the existing storyboard critic with that packet and an explicit phone scope. The planner
722	refuses missing, changed or incomplete movie-derived imagery and computes the report bindings
723	before the paid call. The critic reads every chronological page for both options and returns
724	its independent selection and exact-phone report as JSON in the handback. The director saves
725	the actual response unchanged; Read-only leaves cannot write files. No extraction or mechanical
726	hash supplies a creative verdict. Missing observed actions stay unresolved. Retain an earlier
727	sparse-image response and charge a content follow-up before executing it; it is not a free
728	formatting call or a provider-unavailability event.
729	
730	After measured narration changes the board and preview timing, use the same authorized extractor
731	with `--phone-option current --board out/dispatch/storyboard.json --film out/dispatch/preflight.mp4`
732	and a fresh output directory. It requires the current exact `preflight.json` inspection, edition,
733	board, renderer and movie bytes. It honors only the existing structural release policy; extraction
734	still supplies no verdict. Its separate operation reserves and claims once. Build a fresh ordinary
735	critic packet, then use `claude_runtime.py phone-packet --sequence-current <new index.json>` instead
736	of the two comparison sequence flags. Keep the same packet, state and output arguments. This
737	single-film packet binds the measured current board and film, returns a fresh exact-phone report,
738	and does not choose the silent treatment again. The silent comparison index cannot prove the
739	timed movie; neither phone profile can satisfy the native final profile. Inspect all chronological
740	pages, consolidate one handback and recheck only specific uncertain intervals. Report unresolved
741	observations directly instead of repeatedly viewing the film to pursue approval.
742	
743	For editions from October 24, the fifth critic reservation must bind this final current-phone
744	packet before any spend. Plan the current-phone task, then consume with
745	`run_controller.py consume --resource storyboard_critics --review-packet <exact current-phone packet> --note "final timed phone"`
746	and dispatch the same packet unchanged. The controller validates its current movie, board,
747	chronological sequence and critic assignment before charging; a generic code, pivot or phone
748	label cannot spend the protected slot. Replanning after the charge must retain that exact packet.
749	Do not add owner grants to the daily policy or modify the five-attempt limit during production.
750	
751	A cloud session has no desktop for Computer Use. Use `scripts/phone_playback.py`, real Chromium UI
752	automation at 390x844 with touch input, against the published canonical URL:
753	
754	```sh
755	python scripts/phone_playback.py --edition-id <id> --film-sha256 <reviewed master sha256> --out-dir out/dispatch/phone
756	```
757	
758	It taps the page's own Play control (pause, then play again), taps "tap for sound", samples
759	currentSrc, currentTime, readyState, paused, muted and error while the clock runs, records whether
760	the page received trusted input events, hashes the published master and phone bytes, and saves
761	hashed screenshots. Its `tool` field says browser automation, not Computer Use. Put its
762	`phone_playback.json` in the shipment manifest unchanged. `shipment_check.py` applies every
763	historical assertion plus `claude_playback_problems`. The Codex Computer Use route and its evidence
764	format stay valid. Never fabricate observations. If the page, media or browser fails, production
765	stays active and the real failure is recorded.
766	
767	## Haiku mechanical route (future editions only)
768	
769	Effective for editions from the date in `mechanical_route.effective_from` in `config/claude_runtime.json`.
770	One graded trial showed Haiku at high effort can diagnose and mechanically repair a caption layout gate when
771	the case is strictly specified. The route admits only that shape of work and refuses everything else, which
772	leaves the unchanged Opus assignment. Its evidence is `runs/2026-10-11/experiments/haiku-calibration-1`,
773	including the trial limitations, and it supports no wider claim.
774	
775	- Two tasks only. `code-only-review` runs the storyboard critic read only on named gate tests.
776	  `mechanical-correction` runs the scene builder on named gate tests with one failing case, named acceptance
777	  results, named unchanged controls and named mutation checks.
778	- Only gate tests are in scope: files under `video-engine/tests/` and `scripts/*_test.py`. Renderer source,
779	  art, story, claims, config, prompts, ledgers and every run path are refused, as is the initial authored build.
780	  The three final scorers, the validator, the researcher and the voice director never use this route.
781	- The packet stays the normal complete hash-bound role packet with every current guide. Add a `mechanical`
782	  object to it before planning, naming the task, the exact existing files as `{path, sha256}` pairs and the required fields, and keep expected
783	  findings out of the packet. The scope text may name only those files, and a correction's named results,
784	  controls and mutation checks are non-empty lists of names. Plan with `python scripts/claude_runtime.py plan ... --mechanical-task <task>`.
785	  An admitted plan adds only the Haiku spawn model and effort. The role, brief, packet and controller resource
786	  are the unchanged ones, so reservations, charges and every gate are unchanged. A refusal is not an error to
787	  work around. Plan the same task without the flag.
788	- A Haiku result is never a verdict. Re run the named results, controls and mutation checks yourself, record the
789	  actual agent identity, requested effort and observed usage, keep observed effort and billing unknown where
790	  the host omits them, and let an Opus or Sonnet reviewer judge anything rendered.
791	
792	## Capture authorization
793	
794	For a multi-repository cloud session, the environment setup registers the capture hook at its
795	actual primary workspace before launch with
796	`python scripts/bootstrap_claude_hooks.py --workspace /home/user --prelaunch-router`.
797	The same prelaunch command registers the visual Read/Write guard and actual Write observer at
798	primary settings scope. Agent-frontmatter hooks alone are not a supported cloud registration.
799	Verify all three visual registrations before reserving a visual worker. Its first image/Write
800	probe must receive the actual Write acknowledgment before it reads another image; a missing
801	receipt stops that attempt early. Retain the original failure, every observation and charge;
802	never backfill a Write receipt from a transcript or relabel an incomplete review as approved.
803	The preinstalled router selects the actual production checkout from the command's explicit
804	working directory, including restored checkouts, and runs the unchanged authorization gate.
805	Never replace this registration during an agent turn. The helper preserves model, effort,
806	environment, permissions and unrelated hooks. It replaces only its own earlier registration and
807	points the handler at the active checkout, whose ledger and assets the handler verifies. This is
808	registration, never proof that the host loaded it and never capture authorization. Keep the actual
809	native denial of the harmless capture-form probe before a real capture. If the host has not loaded
810	the registration, retain that observation and restart from the durable checkpoint using the supported
811	routine launch; do not replay synthetic PreToolUse events as a substitute or weaken auto mode.
812	If the host denies registration, preserve the denial and apply the same versioned registration in
813	the authorized environment setup before the next supported launch rather than retrying a denied edit.
814	
815	Every native capture or render command (Remotion stills and renders, preflight, opening compare, cinema proof,
816	render_dispatch) is denied by the PreToolUse hook `scripts/capture_guard.py hook` unless the director has
817	issued a current authorization for that exact command. Use the prepared operator handoff below for
818	the supported operators. It checks occupied output before charging, then binds one fresh render
819	reservation to the exact boards and command. A late-accounting charge never counts.
820	
821	```sh
822	python scripts/capture_guard.py authorize --prepare --state out/dispatch/run_state.json --board out/dispatch/opening-a.json --board out/dispatch/opening-b.json --command "bash scripts/run_with_env.sh python scripts/opening_compare.py --root out/dispatch --state out/dispatch/run_state.json"
823	```
824	
825	For `opening_compare.py`, `preflight_animatic.py`, `cinema_proof.py` and `claude_motion_review.py`, use the
826	prepared operator handoff instead of manually reserving a note and letting the operator reserve
827	again. `authorize --prepare` derives the operation from the exact checkout command, checks the
828	same art, headroom and housekeeping gates, then charges it once. The real host hook consumes
829	the exact authorization, and that operator claims its matching prepaid event once. A phone
830	preview cannot claim a native hero charge; motion extraction has its own exact-film identity.
831	An unchanged operation cannot be prepared again without the existing infrastructure-retry record.
832	Preserve all earlier charges and denied commands.
833	Prepare and execute each exact command before preparing the next one. In particular, prepare and
834	extract option a, collect its result, then prepare and extract option b; two separate preparations
835	must never compete for the single authorization file. The issuer refuses to replace a still usable
836	pending command before charging again. Consumed or stale authorizations are retained byte for byte
837	under `out/dispatch/capture-authorization-history/`; their original reservations remain charged.
838	Before a changed comparison, retain the entire occupied `openings/` directory, including any
839	partial output, in the edition's defect package. Do this before preparing the new capture. Never
840	overwrite it, refund its reservation or rerender an unchanged pair merely to obtain a new identity.
841	Do not create a self-written failure note or request `retry-preflight` to correct an operation
842	label. Fix the actual versioned operator handoff and retain its before/after source evidence.
843	
844	For an actual execution or transport failure after hook consumption, retain the original tool
845	response, spent authorization and reservation. Once the concrete infrastructure fix or supported
846	specific approval is available, follow prompts/phases/repair.md and record `retry-preflight` for
847	that exact operation using the actual failure log. Fund the complete remaining path first, then
848	prepare a fresh charged authorization. Never replay the spent one or refund the failed attempt.
849	
850	```sh
851	python scripts/capture_guard.py authorize --prepare --state out/dispatch/run_state.json --board out/dispatch/storyboard.json --command "bash scripts/run_with_env.sh python scripts/cinema_proof.py --board out/dispatch/storyboard.json --mix out/dispatch/mix.wav --state out/dispatch/run_state.json"
852	```
853	
854	It writes `out/dispatch/capture-authorization.json` only from facts: an unused fresh charged render reservation,
855	passed native headroom, portable housekeeping run with `--apply --fetch --summary --require-headroom` and the
856	computed minimum (its receipt is kept), and genuine recorded authored receipts. The authorization is bound to the
857	exact board, renderer and art hashes and to the listed commands. The hook rechecks them and current headroom,
858	denies unreadable, unresolved or unrelated --props and --board inputs and placeholder art, and consumes each
859	authorized command once, so the next capture needs a new reservation. Builders never capture. Before the first
860	real capture of a run, prove the hook is active with a harmless capture-form command that must be denied,
861	and keep that denial as evidence.
